title: Titanium Handlebar End Plug
alloyReason: Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V (UNS R56400) is specified for Titanium Handlebar End Plug because its 900+ MPa tensile strength allows thin-wall tube shaping without buckling, critical for lightweight frame and component structures. The alpha-beta microstructure delivers 45% higher specific strength than 4140 chromoly steel, translating directly to gram-level weight savings where it matters. Its high-cycle fatigue endurance limit (>500 MPa @10^7 cycles) matches the pedaling load spectrum of Handlebar end plug core screw. This rationale is driven by handlebar end plug core screw and specific design requirements.
process: CNC turning Swiss-type for handlebar hardware geometry
Thread rolling DIN 13-1 6g with Class 6g gauge
Go/No-Go ring gauging with Class 6g gauge
surfaceTreatment: Bead blasting 120 grit Al2O3 for matte finish Ra 1.6-3.2um followed by passive oxide stabilization in DI water — tailored for handlebar end plug application
commonFailures: Thread galling Ti-on-Ti assembly - prevented by MoS2 anti-seize compound and -20% installation torque — critical for handlebar end plug performance

faq.q: How much weight savings does Titanium Handlebar End Plug offer versus steel or aluminum?
faq.a: Titanium Handlebar End Plug fabricated from Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V provides a 40-45% weight reduction versus 4130 chromoly steel (4.43 vs 7.85 g/cm³) at the same strength. Compared to 6061-T6 aluminum, titanium's 3× higher yield strength (830 vs 275 MPa) allows 50-60% thinner walls, resulting in a net weight comparable to aluminum with 4× better fatigue life — critical for handlebar end plug.

faq.q: What material certifications are provided with Titanium Handlebar End Plug?

Dimensional inspection reports and Certificate of Conformance (CoC) are standard. First Article Inspection Reports (FAIR) per AS9102 are available on request for handlebar end plug.
